newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai business hoping for Democrat win in polls.
newsitem.headline: Thai business hoping for Democrat win in polls.

text.p: Thai businessmen and urban voters are pinning their hopes on the Democrat Party to win Sunday's general election and launch an economic revival, analysts said on Thursday.
The Democrats, led by former premier Chuan Leekpai, are seen by many as the party with the most credible economic team among 13 contesting the polls.
Thailand's slowing economy and sluggish exports, which were instrumental in expediting the demise of outgoing premier Banharn Silpa-archa, have emerged as key election issues.

The economy is projected to expand this year at its slowest pace in 10 years at about seven percent against 8.6 in 1995. Exports this year would likely grow only about five percent against 23.6 percent growth in 1995, analysts said.

"Whichever government comes in must make the economy its top priority. The Democrat Party has its economic team as a strong selling point," said Preecha Jarungidanan, director of Chao Phaya Finance and Securities.

The Democrats, who led a government from 1992-1995, have promoted their economic team, led by former finance minister Tarrin Nimmanahaeminda and ex-deputy premier Supachai Panichpakdi, as likely vote winners.
The poll is shaping up as a tight race between the Democrats and the New Aspiration Party (NAP) of outgoing Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, analysts said.
Chavalit said on Wednesday he would recruit professionals, led by a widely respected former banker and Deputy Premier Amnuay Viravan, for his economic "dream team" if elected.

Amnuay, who opted not to run in the election, has yet to commit himself to joining a Chavalit-led coalition and analysts are sceptical that Chavalit would give him a free hand to oversee the economy anyway.
"Nobody knows if Amnuay can work smoothly with elected MPs in a Chavalit-led government. He and these people are not made of the same texture," Preecha of Chao Phaya said.

Most private polls this week put the Democrats and NAP neck and neck in trying to capture the largest bloc of seats in the 393-seat lower House of Representatives that would give one of them a mandate to form a government.
Several polls have projected that the two parties could each win 120-140 seats.
Equities analysts mostly want to see a Democrat win.
"The SET Index will surge 100 points if the Democrats lead the next government but plunge 100-150 points if NAP prevails," said an analyst at a Thai brokerage firm.
"Foreign brokers have recommended sharp trimming of portfolios if NAP is victorious."

But a colleague at General Finance and Securities was more upbeat on NAP's prospects. "I think any new government would have learnt a lesson from the mistakes of its predecessor. If Thai stocks were to fall, it would not be due to politics but more to economic fundamentals," he said.
